newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND PLANS AGENCY TO LIMIT TAX EVASION - MINISTER.
newsitem.headline: POLAND PLANS AGENCY TO LIMIT TAX EVASION - MINISTER.

text.p: The Polish government will draft this year a bill launching a specialist agency to gather and process financial information to combat tax evasion and money laundering, deputy finance minister said on Monday.

"By the end of this year the government will prepare and approve a draft bill on a State Financial Information Agency (PAIF) which should help combat the shadow economy and money laundering," PAP news agency quoted Jan Kubik as saying.
Kubik said that PAIF would study the money sources of dishonest businesspeople and would collect information from financial institutions such as banks and securities houses about large transactions.
He said the government proposed to screen deals exceeding between 20,000 and 50,000 zlotys.

PAP said that a plan approved on Monday by the government's economic committee (KERM) called for setting up a permanent coordinating body comprising central bank, customs, security service, finance and interior ministry officials.
It said that KERM also recommended a 10 percent increase in the number of jobs in agencies dealing with the untaxed shadow economy by the year 2000.
